answer: Stop sybils with a nebula jury and pigment-tagged lotus ballots. Each participant earns a lotus ballot only after its ten collaborations are dyed with a pigment, a tag tied to its funder and those collaborators, unforgeable without repeating collaboration. Ballots float through a nebula of peer juries; when a jury finds two ballots sharing one pigment origin, it folds them into one ballot and slashes every bond behind them, multiplied by the folded count. A lone participant stakes one bond for one ballot, while N copies stake N bonds for the ballot and lose about N squared when exposed.
